elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "IBM shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence".

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: "...and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate" in the same CGL limb.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: "professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000".

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: "where IBM processes, stores, or has access to any data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000" — the trigger covers every category of Customer data, not selected named types, as required.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: "and workers' compensation insurance as required by law".

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: "IBM shall provide certificates of insurance to Customer on request."

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: E&O at USD 2,000,000 exceeds the USD 1,000,000 fallback floor.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Cyber and privacy at USD 5,000,000 exceeds the USD 2,000,000 fallback floor.

reasons: All six preferred elements appear in a single inserted paragraph with the correct amounts, bases (per occurrence / aggregate) and party direction (IBM as insuring party).

The cyber trigger is drafted as "any data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer", which satisfies the requirement that the Customer Data trigger cover every category rather than selected named data types; the drafter correctly noted that "Customer Data" is not a defined term here, so the descriptor avoids an undefined trigger.

Minimality holds: the insertion adds nothing beyond the checklist — the model-language extras ("at its own expense" and the "term and one (1) year thereafter" survival tail) were correctly omitted, and no existing words were deleted or paraphrased. Cited paragraphs (risk of loss, data processing, territorial scope) are reproduced unchanged.

Intent is preserved: the new clause creates a standalone insurance obligation in the miscellaneous section and does not contradict the risk-of-loss allocation in § 14.12, the data-processing terms in § 14.18, or any remedy, cap, or cross-reference; no dangling references or undefined terms are introduced.

Finding kind "missing" is supported — no insurance obligation exists anywhere in the document for a hosting vendor that processes personal information on Customer's behalf, which is walk-away territory under the rule.
